bibliographic_scope.title: Three-Dimensionally Ordered Gold Nanocrystal/Silica Superlattice Thin Films Synthesized via Sol–Gel Self-Assembly
bibliographic_scope.authors: Hongyou Fan; Adam Wright; John Gabaldon; Adrian Rodriguez; C. Jeffrey Brinker; Ying-Bing Jiang

source_interpretation.text: The authors connect acid-controlled silica condensation with film homogeneity. Extensive TEOS aging reduces ordering; BTEE aging has a weaker effect attributed to slower hydrolysis/condensation. This is source interpretation, not a quantitative rate model.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sol–gel and aging discussion

source_interpretation.text: Fcc and Fm3m in the low-angle/TEM discussion concern the nanocrystal superlattice. The10.5/10.8nm values must not be used as atomic Au lattice constants. No atomic coordinates are supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, XRD/TEM and orientation discussion

source_interpretation.text: The source attributes aqueous stability to n-DT/CTAB chain interdigitation and assembly to charge/hydrogen-bond interactions with hydrolyzed silica. These are authors’ mechanisms, not direct surface-coordinate measurements.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Micelles and assembly interpretation

source_interpretation.text: Two acid strengths are listed without sample assignment. BTEE has no separately stated charge. Representative optical/TEM/film-thickness observations remain separate from exact aging labels.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–5, Methods and figure captions

characterization_protocol.XRD: SiemensD500,Ni-filteredCuKα λ1.54Å,θ–2θ,2θ1–10°,step printed0.02,dwell2s. These are low-angle superlattice measurements, not atomic cell refinements.
characterization_protocol.optics: UV–vis curvesFigure1; instrument/spectrum sampling and refractive-index measurement details unreported.

aging_map.scope: Aging at room/ambient temperature in addition to1h stirring;0.07N/1N acid and spin rates not individually allocated.

structure_scales.atomic: No preferred atomic-Au orientation in wide-angleXRD; no atomic cell dimensions/coordinates.

future_applications: Semiconductor/magneticNCarrays,memory,laser,molecularelectronics,SERS are outlook/context, not additional demonstrated material preparations or property tests.

references.note: 46numbered references read; full cited works unreviewed.

limitations: Complete five-page main, Scheme 1, Figures 1–3 and all 46 numbered references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
HAuCl4 hydration, reagent purities, aqueous phase-transfer duration, reduction temperature and numeric addition rate are not reported. The visible phase-transfer color endpoint is explicit.

The source gives TEOS (0.08 g) or BTEE without an independently stated BTEE amount. BTEE charge remains unknown; its two aging observations are retained as supporting routes rather than complete direct recipes.
HCl is 0.07 N or 1 N, 0.05 mL. The choice is not assigned to each film/aging specimen; no extra factorial experiments or inferred molar concentrations are created.
Quick-heating temperature/time for chloroform removal, NC stock concentration after clarification, spin duration, substrate cleaning and precise spin rate per specimen are unknown.
The 1 h room-temperature mixing precedes separately reported 0/5/24 h aging. No-aging means no additional aging, not absence of the 1 h sol–gel mixing.

Low-angle fcc parameters around 10.5/10.8 nm and Fm3m describe the nanocrystal superlattice mesostructure, not the atomic Au unit cell. No atomic coordinates or atomic Au lattice constant are supplied.
Representative TEM/optical/film-thickness results lack an exact aging/spin-rate/acid-strength crosswalk. They are supporting specimen contexts, not copied into each aging experiment.
Casting up to25 µm and micromolded stripe/dot patterns are supporting contexts: complete casting/micromolding schedules are not supplied. Cited methods remain unreviewed.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.
